newsitem.title: MONACO: MOTOR RACING-MOSELEY SAYS NO GOING BACK ON REGULATION CHANGES.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-MOSELEY SAYS NO GOING BACK ON REGULATION CHANGES.

text.p: New rules covering grooved tyres and narrow chassis will be brought in next year despite opposition from drivers such as current championship leader Jacques Villeneuve, International Motoring Federation (FIA) president Max Moseley said on Saturday.

Speaking at a news conference shortly before qualifying for Sunday's Monaco Grand Prix, Mosley said the Formula One changes made on safety grounds, had been proosed by the team's engineers, agreed unanimously and passed by the FIA's world council.
"There is no going back now," he said. "And any rumours going around in the paddock that suggest otherwise are wrong."

Mosley said also that criticism of the grooved tyres by world championship leading Canadian Jacques Villeneuve was entirely to be expected from any driver who wanted to maintain as much speed as possible from his car.
"It is our responsibility to worry about safety, not his," he explained.
He said that the new rules were introduced to improve safety standards by slowing the cars in corners.

He said the development of tyres had been the single most influential factor in improving the performances of the cars in recent years and that explained why the FIA were introducing grooved tyres. This phenomenon had been aggravated this year by the tyre war between Bridgestone and Goodyear, he said.
Mosley said one in 10 accidents during the 1960's was fatal, but the corresponding statistic now was one in 300.
He said also that the introduction of padding around a driver's head in the cockpit had saved Ducthman Jos Verstappen when he crashed at the Belgian Grand Prix at Spa-Francorchamps last year.
"His accident would have been fatal if he had been driving a car as they were two years earlier before the padding had been introduced," said Mosley.
